messages:
maria: Heads up — we started seeing a spike in pod disconnects from model-serving pods in eastus2 about ~10:05 UTC. Pods report ECONNRESET to S3 and some GRPC streams drop.
jonathan: Seeing the same on the monitoring dashboard. Src: gpu-pool-eastus2. Packet loss + reconnect storms. Could be NAT/conntrack exhaustion again.
lee: I just ssh'd into a node and ran conntrack -S. cntr summary shows ~215k entries on one node.
maria: Can you paste the exact output?
lee: conntrack -S | grep "established" -A2
# output:
# entries    215842
# found 215842 flow entries

lee: sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max -> 262144
lee: conntrack -L | tail -n3 -> a lot of 10.0.x.y:randomport -> 52.170.x.y:443 ESTABLISHED from model-worker processes
ashley: Those are outbound ephemeral ports to S3/qsproxy for checkpoints. We kicked off a batch of checkpoint uploads around 10:02 causing connection churn.
maria: Do we have short-lived connections (no keepalive) from the uploader lib? I thought uploads were chunked with keepalives.
jonathan: Apparently the uploader opens new connection per chunk (4096 bytes). That explains the high ephemeral port churn per pod.
infra-bot: Incident runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/conntrack-exhaustion (runbook auto-suggest)
lee: Immediate mitigation: 1) throttle checkpointing job to stagger uploads 2) increase nf_conntrack_max to 524288 on eastus2 nodes 3) restart kube-proxy to clear stale NAT entries only if safe.
ashley: Increasing nf_conntrack_max buys us headroom but not a fix. We should also reduce creation rate of ephemeral connections.
maria: I rolled a quick patch to the uploader to enable HTTP keep-alive and connection pooling. Deploying now to gpu-pool-eastus2 canary.
jonathan: For the short term, will cordon/evict + recreate nodes help? If we cycle nodes, conntrack table resets per node and pod placement spreads traffic.
lee: We drained one node and it temporarily recovered. But this is risky at scale for GPU workloads.
ashley: Cloud provider has a per-node SNAT port limit too. On Azure our available ephemeral ports per node are ~64k. If each pod creates many concurrent outbound sockets, we hit SNAT port exhaustion sooner.
maria: Good point — bumping nf_conntrack doesn't change ephemeral port arithmetic. We should implement node-local egress (SNAT pool) or use an egress gateway to reduce SNAT churn.
jonathan: Timeline: Can we do these in order? 1) throttle checkpoint job immediately (done) 2) deploy uploader patch with keep-alive (maria deploying) 3) bump nf_conntrack_max across nodepool (lee to run ansible) 4) add node-local egress/egress gateway (planning)
lee: I pushed a quick sysctl change to a test daemonset for nodes in the canary pool: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288. Confirming it applied to 4/4 test nodes.
infra-bot: Alert suppressed for "conntrack-high" after mitigation step set by maria
ashley: Longer term proposals: - instrument conntrack exporter (Prometheus) per node - enforce client-side connection pooling in all data-plane libs - use NAT gateway with larger port range or per-node SNAT per-pod mapping (if provider supports) - evaluate the use of IPVS + conntrack-timeout tuning
maria: Also adding a runtime config to limit parallel uploads per model-worker to 4.
jonathan: Note about RDMA: RDMA traffic bypasses kernel TCP stack for RDMA verbs; not related here. But keep an eye — any network driver updates might affect conntrack behavior for TCP fallback.
lee: Action items assigned: maria (patch + rollout), ashley (egress gateway design doc), jonathan (monitoring dashboard update + alert thresholds), lee (sysctl rollout + conntrack exporter PoC).
ashley: I'll draft the egress gateway doc and add cost estimate for NAT gateway vs managed egress.
maria: I'll confirm whether any A/B model clients still do per-chunk connections and update the SDK.
jonathan: Closing loop — once patch is fully rolled and conntrack counts drop, we'll uncordon remaining nodes. ETA 2h for full mitigation.
lee: Current conntrack count on patched canary nodes: ~38k -> good downward trend.
maria: Thanks everyone. Adding follow-ups to infra board and will schedule a blameless postmortem to capture root cause and long-term mitigations. :thumbsup:
